nodes.summary: The gradient descent exponent is the supremum, in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, of the set of real numbers $c$ such that some step schedule $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ achieves a uniform last-iterate rate with exponent $c$. In particular, it is $-\infty$ if there is no such $c$, and $+\infty$ if these exponents are unbounded above.

nodes.summary: The silver ratio is the real number $\rho = 1 + \sqrt{2}$.

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Hilbert space, $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x_0 \in E$. If every step size is $0$, then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the $k$-th gradient descent iterate of $f$ from $x_0$ equals $x_0$.
nodes.title: Gradient descent with zero step sizes stays put

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Hilbert space, $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$, $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ a sequence of step sizes and $x_0 \in E$. The gradient descent trajectory of $f$ from $x_0$ with steps $s$ is the sequence $(x_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ starting at $x_0$ with $x_{k+1} = x_k - s_k \nabla f(x_k)$.
nodes.title: Gradient descent with a step schedule

nodes.summary: The step schedule with every step size equal to $1$ achieves a uniform last-iterate rate with exponent $1$.
nodes.title: Constant unit steps achieve exponent one

nodes.title: Uniform last-iterate rate of a step schedule

nodes.summary: A function $f : E \to \mathbb{R}$ on a real Hilbert space $E$ is unit-smooth convex if it is convex, differentiable, and its gradient is $1$-Lipschitz: $\lVert \nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y) \rVert \le \lVert x - y \rVert$ for all $x, y \in E$.

nodes.summary: The silver exponent is $\log_2 \rho = \log \rho / \log 2$, where $\rho = 1 + \sqrt{2}$ is the silver ratio.

nodes.summary: The silver step schedule is the sequence $s_t = 1 + \rho^{\nu_2(t + 1) - 1}$ for $t \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\rho = 1 + \sqrt{2}$ is the silver ratio and $\nu_2(n)$ is the exponent of $2$ in the prime factorization of $n$.
